text: El partido entre Harbour City y Seabrook Town terminó 2-4, con una remontada impresionante de Seabrook en los minutos finales [#1882]. Harbour City comenzó ganando con dos goles, incluyendo uno de Marek Barros, quien brilló con un gol, 2 asistencias y 9 intercepciones, logrando una nota de 9.8 [#975]. Sin embargo, Seabrook dominó en tiros, posesión y corners, controlando el juego y generando más oportunidades claras para marcar. El punto de inflexión fue la expulsión de Joon Whitfield de Harbour City al minuto 43, que debilitó su defensa [#871]. Seabrook cambió su estrategia para presionar y atacar por las bandas, y Kian Romano marcó dos goles seguidos en tiempo extra tras rápidas jugadas de contraataque, asegurando la victoria de su equipo [#1882] [#1906].

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in es

- Seabrook Town had 4 goals with a total xG of 3.48 vs Harbour City's 2 goals and xG 1.0, showing more effective attacks [#1882, #1906].
- Marek Barros (Harbour City) had a key role with 1 goal, 2 assists, 5 key passes, 9 interceptions and a 9.8 rating [#975].
- Seabrook Town's possession was 53.4% with higher shots (22) and corners (9), indicating control of the game [#team_stats].
- A red card for Joon Whitfield (Harbour City) at 43' likely impacted the team's defense [#871].
- Kian Romano scored twice in added time (90+2', 90+3') to secure Seabrook Town's late comeback and win [#1882, #1906].

- Seabrook Town's winning goals late in the match were a result of quick regains and effective counter-attacks, exemplified by Kian Romano's 90+2' goal after a 6.7-second build-up involving just two passes starting from a regain [1881,1882]. This indicates Seabrook used fast transitions to exploit Harbour City's higher pressing and more direct play as they chased the game.
- Harbour City's first goal at 45' came after a prolonged patient build-up of 56.7 seconds involving 17 passes, consistent with their 4-2-3-1 formation and patient short passing style under coach Tomasz Rhee. The goal was assisted by Marek Barros via a through ball, showing their methodical pattern breaking down Seabrook's 3-4-3 defensive shape [904,905].
- Seabrook Town, playing a wide 3-4-3 formation with emphasis on crossing, leveraged wide play and directness following their tactical change at 65', where they increased press intensity, directness, and line height significantly. This adjustment led to three late goals and increased field tilt to 63.3% in the second half, reflecting a more aggressive, wide attacking pattern to overload and stretch Harbour City's compact 4-2-3-1 structure [1361, 1447, 1448].
- Harbour City struggled under sustained pressure in the second half, as shown by a drop in possession (44.6%) and field tilt (36.7%) and increased turnovers. Their patient style was disrupted by Seabrook's quicker press and wider attacking approach, forcing Harbour to switch to a higher press and more direct play very late (90+2'), but by then Seabrook's counter-attacking efficiency had already turned the match [1884].
